entities.label: TextOfTheConstitution
entities.rationale: The text of the Constitution is a specific information artifact — a pattern of linguistic content that can be copied, instantiated on multiple physical substrates (paper, digital, etc.), and transmitted across time. This is the canonical BFO typing for a document's content: a generically dependent continuant (BFO_0000031). It is an individual because it refers to the specific text of the US Constitution, not a kind of text. It can be typed under the existing working:Statute class, which is already a subclass of BFO_0000031.

relations.rationale: The text of the Constitution is an instance of the Statute class (a generically dependent continuant representing legal document content), which already exists in the working ontology.
The text is part of the US Constitution individual already in the ontology. The textual content is a proper part of the broader constitutional artifact/document individual.

open_questions: Should 'the text of the Constitution' be distinguished from 'the Constitution' (working:USConstitution) as a separate individual, or should working:USConstitution itself serve as the text? Currently USConstitution is typed BFO_0000031, so it may already represent the text; a part-of relation is proposed but merging the two individuals is an alternative.

Is there a need to distinguish the constitutional text as a generically dependent continuant (the information content) from any particular physical inscription (a material entity like a parchment document)? If so, a concretization relation could be added linking the text to its physical bearers.
proposal.rationale_summary: The phrase 'the text of the Constitution' refers to the specific linguistic-informational content of the US Constitution — a pattern that can be copied across multiple physical substrates without loss of identity. In BFO 2020, this typing falls squarely under generically dependent continuant (BFO_0000031), whose hallmark is that it depends generically on some material bearer but is not tied to any one particular bearer. The existing working:Statute class (already a subclass of BFO_0000031) is the most appropriate parent. A new individual working:TextOfTheConstitution is minted because the utterance refers to a specific text, not to a general kind. A BFO_0000050 (part of) relation links it to the already-existing working:USConstitution individual, since the text is a component of the broader constitutional artifact. An open question is raised about whether working:USConstitution already plays the same role, to avoid redundancy.
